title: The light in the sun (15.7–15.15)
hook: Krishna says the brightness of the sun, the moon and the fire is his
tomorrow: The two and the one beyond (15.16–15.20)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the tree with roots above. The whole world of change as an upside-down fig, cut with the axe of not clinging. Your line was upside-down tree. Did you loosen one finger? Day two hundred eleven.

Think about the last time you ate a warm meal. The grain grew in sunlight. The moon pulled the tides and the farmers timed the planting by it. The fire cooked it. And then, somewhere inside you, another kind of fire digested it and turned it into you. The whole thing is a chain of light and heat, from the sky to your stomach. Chapter fifteen walks down that exact chain, link by link, and at every link Krishna says the same thing: that's me.
screen: `SUNLIGHT IN THE GRAIN.` → `FIRE IN THE POT.` → `FIRE IN YOU.`

segments.voice: It starts with you. Verse seven: a fragment of me, eternal, became the living being in the world of life. Mamaivamsha: a part of my own self. It draws the senses and the mind to itself. Verse eight gives a gentle picture: when that living self takes a body and leaves it, it carries the senses along, the way the wind carries scent from a flower. You can't see it go, but something has moved. Verse ten admits most people don't notice it, staying or leaving. Those with the eye of wisdom do. Then the chain of light. Verse twelve: the brightness in the sun that lights the whole world, and the light in the moon, and the light in fire: know that light as mine. Verse thirteen: entering the earth, I hold up all beings with my energy. Becoming the juicy moon, soma, I nourish the plants. Verse fourteen: becoming the fire of digestion in living bodies, joined with the breath going in and out, I digest the four kinds of food. So God, in this chapter, isn't only far off. God is the warmth in your belly after dinner. And verse fifteen brings it all the way home. I am seated in the heart of all. From me come memory, knowledge, and their loss. I am what all the Vedas are trying to know. Your line today is in Krishna's voice. When the Gita says I am the light, it's the divine speaking, and the verse asks you to see that light everywhere, from the sun to your own heart. That's the word today: the light in the sun.
screen: `A FRAGMENT OF ME, IN YOU.` · `LIGHT IN SUN, MOON AND FIRE.` · `THE FIRE THAT DIGESTS YOUR FOOD.` · `SEATED IN THE HEART OF ALL.` · then, large: `THE LIGHT IN THE SUN.`

segments.voice: Sit, and trace the chain in your own body. Feel any warmth: your hands, your chest, your belly. That warmth started as sunlight. Follow it back: from your belly to the meal, from the meal to the field, from the field to the sun. Then turn around and follow it home again, to the center of your chest. Rest there, where verse fifteen says the light is seated. The bell holds the time.
The light in the sun. Gita fifteen, twelve: the brightness in the sun, the moon and the fire is Krishna's light; verse fifteen says that light is seated in every heart.
screen: `THE LIGHT IN THE SUN — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: I am the light. Krishna's words. Today, before you eat, pause for one breath and think of the chain: sun, field, fire, you. Day two hundred eleven.

screen: `DAY 211 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE TWO AND THE ONE BEYOND.`

howItsDone: Some Hindu families and communities recite Gita chapter fifteen before meals; verse 15.14 describes the divine as the fire of digestion, which makes it a natural mealtime reading.

fork.setup: Krishna wants a picture for how the self carries the senses from one body to the next. what does he choose?
options: wind carrying scent from a flower.
fork.reveal: wind carrying scent. you can't see the scent move, but it's gone from one place and present in another.

original.note: Sanskrit: tejas, brilliance, radiance; the brightness in the sun that Krishna calls his own in Gita 15.12.

trapdoor: what you thought: 'I am the light' is a slogan.
what it means: in Gita 15 the divine says the light in sun, moon and fire, and the fire in your body, are his, and he sits in every heart.
what a scholar hears: 15.12–15.15 move from cosmic light to vaishvanara, the digestive fire joined with prana and apana, to the heart; 15.7 calls the living being 'mamaivamsha', a part of me.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 15.7–15.11 (a fragment of me; the self carries the senses like wind carries scent)

Bhagavad Gita 15.15 (seated in the heart of all)

notes: howItsDone says some families recite chapter 15 before meals: a known custom in some communities (e.g., parts of South India, ISKCON), but confirm phrasing.
Original word is tejas (15.12: yad aditya-gatam tejo); confirm spelling and pronunciation.
The carry 'I am the light' is framed explicitly as Krishna's words, so it doesn't read as the listener claiming divinity.
